analysis.title: Marketcolour + Cross-Asset Outlook / Copper / ASML Fieldtrip / Airtel (I) / GTT & Technip, 19 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities closed mixed on the prior session: SPX -23bps to 7323, NDX +42bps to 27116, RTY +46bps to 27236. Energy fell 325bps and Consumer Discretionary rose 184bps. Hyperscalers were firm (AMZN +3%, GOOG +1%).
In Europe, AI capex names held up (ASML +2%, STM +2%, IFX +1%) while most other sectors fell. Materials and energy led the decline, following a global drop in commodity prices.

Cross-asset outlook is overweight SPX, TOPIX, 10Y UST and Gilts, and underweight USD high yield. GS stays modestly pro-risk but wants more balance as nominal and earnings growth approach a peak after the 2026 AI capex boom and energy-driven inflation boost.

Near-term risks GS lists are AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and persistent fiscal concerns. In 2027 the balance between slowing growth and rates relief should drive risk appetite.

GS argues a peak in nominal growth need not end the bull market if inflation falls and real growth stays resilient. Easing energy prices and normalising inflation should limit further tightening and let bond yields decline gradually.

Copper fell 5% in the prior session on global growth concerns (BCOM -2%), bearish Chinese demand feedback from the Shanghai CESCO conference, and expected US exports, which triggered heavy short-selling on SHFE.

GS bull case on copper: direct AI copper demand holds because capex is committed, scrap stays tight for at least two quarters, mine supply does not rebound in 2027, State Grid tenders are rising into year end, and the US administration is expected to be proactive on trade policy.

GS expects the Fed to hike 25bp in December 2026 and March 2027 to a peak range of 4.25-4.5%, then cut gradually from November 2027 to a terminal range of 3.25-3.5%. It expects the ECB to hike 25bp in December to a 2.75% peak, then ease to a 2.25% terminal rate in 4Q27.

ASML fieldtrip takeaways: strong momentum in High NA and its ecosystem, a deep competitive moat, multiple avenues for output optimisation, strong momentum in installed base management and upgrades, and GS views Match Act concerns as overdone.

Airtel (Africa) initiated with a 260p price target (15% upside, 15x EBITDA). GS expects Airtel Money revenue ex-FX CAGR of about 26% over FY26-31E, driven by penetration of the subscriber base and rising ARPU as customers move into payments and financial services.

GS identifies about 280 mtpa of LNG capacity reaching FID across 2025-30, up about 52 mtpa or 23% from about 228 mtpa in TP2026. GTT is the preferred LNG exposure (Buy, EUR 210 12-month PT, 12.4% upside). Technip Energies is removed from the Buy list, mainly on valuation after strong share-price performance.

UniCredit and Germany reached broad agreement over Commerzbank. Finance Minister Klingbeil said UniCredit made clear commitments on Germany as a business location, Commerzbank employee rights and dialogue with the works council.

NKT Q3 operating EBITDA was 4% below consensus, with weaker top line in Transmission and Distribution on tough comps and timing effects. Guidance was maintained, with NKT expecting the high end of the range, implying about EUR 430m vs consensus EUR 424m, a c.1% upgrade.

Halma 1H organic growth was +12.3% vs consensus +11.5%, a 5% beat driven by Safety. E&A, which contains photonics, missed. Photonics grew 30% in 1H and is still guided to about 30% for the full year. Guidance was unchanged.

GTA 6 launched with over $1.65B in preorder sales, about 75% on PlayStation 5 and the rest on Xbox Series S and X. Preloads caused record traffic, including the largest single network event in Comcast's history and a record peak at Virgin Media O2.

market_movers.rationale: Airtel Africa initiated with 15% upside at 15x EBITDA. Airtel Money is expected to grow revenue ex-FX at about 26% CAGR over FY26-31E.
GTT is GS's preferred LNG exposure. The 12-month PT implies 12.4% upside as LNG FID capacity forecasts rise.
Technip Energies is removed from the Buy list, mainly on valuation after strong share-price performance, though it remains well positioned in LNG.
Fieldtrip points to strong High NA momentum, a deep competitive moat and strong installed base and upgrades business. GS sees Match Act concerns as overdone.

sector_views.rationale: LNG capacity reaching FID in 2025-30 was raised about 23% to c.280 mtpa, which supports GTT.

earnings_insights: NKT Q3: operating EBITDA 4% below consensus, reported. Transmission and Distribution revenue was weaker than expected. Guidance was maintained with the high end of the range expected, implying about EUR 430m vs consensus EUR 424m.

Halma (HLMA) 1H: reported organic growth +12.3% vs consensus +11.5%. Safety outperformed and E&A missed. Photonics grew +30% in 1H and is guided to about +30% for the full year, with guidance unchanged.
